subject: Control plane backpressure during private upgrade — stabilization plan & customer note
messages:
From: Dave Rogers <dave.rogers@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Inc: control plane timeouts during upgrade window

Evelyn/Marcus,

We're seeing widespread 503/504 timeouts from the private control plane starting ~02:07 UTC (roughly 0:07 local). Impact: connector health checks failing, job backfills paused, and a number of end-user requests timing out. This began immediately after the maintenance window your team initiated at 02:00 UTC.

Attached is a short snippet from our side (ops-log-snippet.txt) showing repeated "controlplane: timeout waiting for response" and connector reconnect loops. We have some production SLAs impacted and would like an urgent triage call.

Can you confirm whether the upgrade completed or if there was a rollback? Any immediate mitigation we can apply on our side (rate-limit clients, disable noncritical connectors)?

Thanks,

Dave Rogers
SRE Lead, Acme Health
Attachment: ops-log-snippet.txt (text/plain)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Dave Rogers <dave.rogers@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Inc: control plane timeouts during upgrade window

Hi Dave — thanks for the heads up and the log snippet. Short update from our side: we initiated an automated rollback at ~09:30 PST after observing persistent request-queue growth on the control plane_processes during the upgrade. The rollback completed but you may still see elevated timeouts while the system drains.

Triage / immediate actions we have taken:
- Rolled back to previous control plane image at 09:30 PST.
- Temporarily increased control-plane replica count in your cluster to reduce request queueing.
- Pushed a short-term runtime patch that tightens per-request timeouts to prevent long tail tasks from clogging worker threads.
- Applied a client-side advisory: please throttle non-critical connector traffic for the next 30m if possible.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) 30-minute bridge at 10:00 PST to walk through logs and confirm stability (I will send a calendar invite).
2) If stable, we will schedule a staged re-upgrade during a narrower window with canary traffic routing.

I've attached a short stabilization plan summary (redwood-stabilization-plan-v1.pdf) for your ops team with exact knobs and recommended client-side rate limits.

We appreciate the quick escalation — I will be on the bridge and Marcus will lead the patch notes review.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-stabilization-plan-v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Subject: Re: Inc: control plane timeouts during upgrade window

Thanks Dave — adding a few technical details from our side and the fixes we pushed live on the bridge.

What we observed: during the upgrade one of the shutdown hooks blocked on an in-flight KV flush which prevented worker threads from returning to the pool; this caused a backlog and eventual 504s for new requests. The automated rollback removed the new image, but the backlog persisted until we reduced max concurrent requests and increased replicas.

What we patched on the bridge (live at ~10:05 PST):
- Forced soft timeouts on long-running internal RPCs (config change: control.rpc.timeout=3s).
- Temporarily lowered probe frequency for non-critical connectors to reduce pressure.
- Increased control-plane replica count from 3 -> 5 for your cluster to absorb burst traffic.
- Adjusted the healthcheck window to avoid flapping during drain (healthcheck.window=30s).

Notes / runbook links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=abcdef123 (internal runbook excerpt)

We will continue to monitor for 24 hours and schedule a staged re-deploy with a canary that exercises short-lived flows first. We also have a follow-up engineering change to replace blocking flush hooks with async checkpoints; target for that change is next week.

If you can keep non-critical connectors throttled for 1 hour it will help our drain. Apologies for the disruption — we'll own the timeline and keep you closely updated.

—Marcus
Senior Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 6 Dec 2026 16:48:00 -0500
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: control plane backpressure on 2026-12-05 — Acme Health

Hi Dave/Priya,

Thank you again for your patience while we worked through the upgrade regression. This note summarizes what happened, the root cause, immediate mitigations, and the timeline for a permanent fix. Please treat this as the customer-facing post-incident communication; I can redact technical details if you'd like a version for your execs.

Summary / impact:
- Incident start: 2026-12-05 02:07 UTC — elevated 503/504 from private control plane observed after a scheduled upgrade.
- Scope: intermittent timeouts for connector health checks and a subset of user-facing requests for approximately 45 minutes.
- Mitigation: automated rollback at 09:30 PST, throttling and replica increase, runtime soft-timeout patch; full user-facing recovery by ~10:20 PST.

Root cause (short): a blocking shutdown hook in the new control plane image caused worker thread starvation under upgrade conditions, leading to request queue growth and tail latency.

Actions taken (completed):
- Immediate rollback to prior image (completed).
- Emergency runtime patch to enforce per-request soft timeouts (completed).
- Increased replicas to handle burst pressure (completed).
- Client advisory to throttle non-critical connectors for the short term (completed).

Planned/next actions (owner / ETA):
- Replace blocking flush hook with async checkpoint (Engineering, target: 2026-12-12).
- Add automated canary gating on shutdown hooks for upgrades (Platform, target: 2026-12-15).
- Postmortem document and timeline (attached: postmortem-acme-20261205.pdf).

We propose a short maintenance window next week (Thu 2026-12-10 02:00 UTC) to roll forward the fix behind a canary and verify under controlled traffic. Please confirm if this slot works for Acme Health or propose alternatives.

I'm attaching the postmortem and the stabilization plan we used (postmortem-acme-20261205.pdf, redwood-stabilization-plan-v1.pdf). If you'd like a 1:1 review with our engineering leads, we can schedule that as well.

Please let us know whether you'd like this ticket closed or any additional follow-up items.

Thanks again — we'll keep monitoring and will notify you before the maintenance window.

Best regards,

Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachments: postmortem-acme-20261205.pdf (application/pdf), redwood-stabilization-plan-v1.pdf (application/pdf)
